order_note: Predecessor SQL 141 (owner 2026-11-13: pay a vendor from a check or from a payroll payment; "New migration" and "Record in payroll"). The API login (checksops, subject to row-level security) cannot read another organization's vendor_tenants row (SQL 141's aws_select_vendor_tenants: the vendor's own members and the platform owner), so the send endpoint could not refuse a payee whose organization is no longer marked a vendor. SQL 165 creates public.aws_vendor_payees_for_tenant(uuid) (plpgsql, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path public, row_security off; EXECUTE checksops and the owner only): refused (forbidden) unless the caller is a member of the tenant; otherwise the tenant's live tenant_vendor_payees links with vendor_tenant_id, vendor_name, partner_code_used, added_at, is_vendor, subscription_status and payable. Reads only; nothing of SQL 141 changes, so SQL 165 does not supersede it. It also lets public.payroll_runs name a vendor: vendor_tenant_id uuid (nullable; payroll_runs_vendor_tenant_id_fkey to tenants; partial index payroll_runs_vendor_tenant_idx; column INSERT for checksops), stakeholder_account_id NOT NULL dropped (its foreign key unchanged), and payroll_runs_one_payee_check (num_nonnulls of the two = 1). Every payroll_runs policy (SQL 136's money-write gates included) and table grant is unchanged. The engine refuses SQL 165 (predecessors_applied) unless SQL 141 reads applied. The spec prerequisites are the file's own (55000 sql165_prerequisite_missing); the applying login must read tenants, vendor_tenants and tenant_vendor_payees past row security (sql165_definer_cannot_read) and own payroll_runs (sql165_not_payroll_owner). Expected pre-state in both environments: the function, the column, both constraints and the index absent, and payroll_runs.stakeholder_account_id uuid NOT NULL with no default (release sql165 v1: 3a6d086e37c04740397c0b6a99d558ed0a5e907c296f8a99a71ae323acdca248). The release-sql141-production-apply test's guard that no other repository SQL references SQL 141's objects now allows exactly this file (owner-approved new migration), and asserts it only reads them. The API (moov-send.mjs vendor recipients, the vendor payee endpoints in workflow-rpc.mjs, the platform-owner vendor flag) ships after this through its own guarded path; no API, Lambda or SPA change is part of this pin.
